nodes.name: One-pot hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The nickel selenides with different stoichiometric number (NiSe or NiSe-V) were prepared via a one-pot hydrothermal method, which can be directly obtained via controlling the ratio of Ni²⁺ and SeO₂ sources owing to the small difference in electronegativity for Ni and Se. Firstly, Ni²⁺ forms nickel-hydrazine complex upon adding of hydrazine hydrate, reacts with the selenium-containing solution at high temperature.
nodes.source_text: As schematically shown in Figure 1a, the nickel selenides with different stoichiometric number (NiSe or NiSe-V) were prepared via a one-pot hydrothermal method, which can be directly obtained via controlling the ratio of Ni²⁺ and SeO₂ sources...

nodes.characterization_summary: PtSA-NiSe-V shows hexagonal Ni0.85Se (PDF#18-0888) peaks at 33.1°, 44.9°, 50.5° with (101) plane positive shift of 0.2°; no Pt or metallic Pt peaks detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the X-ray powder diffraction patterns (XRD), the major reflection peaks of PtSA-NiSe and NiSe composites at around 32.7°, 44.3° and 49.9° can be assigned to the (101), (102) and (110) planes of hexagonal NiSe (PDF#02-0892) ... Notably, no new peaks corresponding to Pt appear in the XRD patterns of PtSA-NiSe-V and PtSA-NiSe, indicating a high degree of dispersion of Pt single atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: PtSA-NiSe-V shows isolated bright Pt single atoms in Ni vacancies; lattice fringes of (101) plane at 0.27 nm spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spherical aberration corrected transmission electron microscope (ACSTEM) could be directly employed to demonstrate the arrangement of Ni atoms ... the high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and AC-STEM measurements were employed to characterize the isolated states of Pt atoms in PtSA-NiSe-V and PtSA-NiSe.

nodes.characterization_summary: PtSA-NiSe-V shows Pt content of ≈3.2 wt.% and ≈1.13 at.%; Pt atoms enriched around surface edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDX analysis estimates a Pt content of ≈3.2 wt.% and ≈1.13 at.% indicating the Pt atoms were atomically dispersed (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: PtSA-NiSe-V Pt loading 3.2 wt.%, PtSA-NiSe 2.7 wt.%
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of Pt atoms was further confirmed by the coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES). The PtSA-NiSe-V shows the same Pt loading amount of 3.2 wt.% which is consistent with the EDX results, slightly higher than that of PtSA-NiSe (2.7 wt.%).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe-V shows strong signal at g=2.26 from Ni cationic vacancies; PtSA-NiSe-V shows no vacancy signal as vacancies filled by Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EPR spectrum of NiSe-V in Figure 2a exhibits a strong signal at g = 2.26, which is caused by Ni cationic vacancies, while the PtSA-NiSe-V shows no cationic vacancies signal observed in EPR.

nodes.characterization_summary: PtSA-NiSe-V and PtSA-NiSe Pt 4f7/2 at ~72.3 eV (shifted higher than Pt/C 71.2 eV, indicating lower electron density); Se 3d peaks negative shift after Pt loading due to Pt→Se charge transfer; no Ni 2p shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The main peaks (Pt4f7/2) in PtSA-NiSe-V and PtSA-NiSe are approximately 72.3 eV, which shift toward a lower binding energy, suggesting the strong electrons transfer effect ... No obvious change of the peak positions and line shape after the loading of atomic Pt can be observed, indicating no charge transfer between Ni and Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: PtSA-NiSe-V shows highest white-line intensity indicating most oxidized Pt 5d states and positive threshold energy shift vs Pt foil.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The quantitative white-line intensity of PtSA-NiSe-V and PtSA-NiSe is higher than that of Pt foil, suggesting that the single atoms are anchored in the positive charge states.

nodes.characterization_summary: No Pt-Pt peak at 2.5 Å; Pt-Se coordination at ~2.2 Å confirms Pt-Se bridge; no Pt-Ni bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transformed k2 weighted χ(k)-function of EXAFS spectrum in Figure 2f shows the absence of the expected peak corresponding to metallic Pt-Pt interaction at 2.5Å ... The characteristic peak around 2.2Å can be assigned to the Pt-Se feature.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl values: PtSA-NiSe-V 25.99 mF cm^-2, PtSA-NiSe 22.85 mF cm^-2, NiSe-V 18.54 mF cm^-2, NiSe 15.23 mF cm^-2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl values of PtSA-NiSe-V, PtSA-NiSe, NiSe-V and NiSe catalysts are 25.99, 22.85, 18.54 and 15.23 mF cm^-2, respectively (Figure S11).

nodes.characterization_summary: PtSA-NiSe-V shows smallest charge transfer resistance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements suggest that PtSA-NiSe-V has the smallest charge transfer resistance than that of PtSA-NiSe, NiSe-V and NiSe.

nodes.characterization_summary: PtSA-NiSe-V maintains urchin-like morphology after Pt deposition, no significant morphological changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After depositing Pt, no significant changes in morphology were observed for the NiSe and NiSe-V nanostructures, and the urchin-like shape remained unchanged (Figure 1b and S2).
